selection_rationale: candidate-A1 (Verifier–Agent Co-Design) is selected: it directly addresses a high-impact unresolved gap (the verifier tax), received a positive 'pass' critic verdict, is experimentally falsifiable, and is feasible within available compute/testbed constraints while aligning tightly with the programme remit (NetOps safety/reliability).
unresolved_uncertainties: Verifier–agent interface underspecified (message/API format, timing, error semantics) and potential for hand-tuned designs to bias outcomes.
Emulator/testbed ecological validity: results may overfit to chosen synthetic topologies; generalization to production networks is uncertain.
Missing pre-registered power/sample-size justification and lack of exact LLM/model identifiers, hyperparameters, and seeds.
Potential sensitivity of results to co-design implementation choices (feedback format/intensity, beam/pruning policies) and to the particular verifier chosen.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Specify exact verifier implementation or API (e.g., Batfish/NetKAT or custom) and formally define verifier feedback primitives (constraints, counterexamples, pruning signals).
Provide full emulator/testbed specification and task-corpus generation scripts; include at least two topology classes and publish trace/emulator configuration to justify ecological validity.
Pre-register sample-size/power calculation, exact LLM model identifiers and hyperparameters (version, temperature), random seeds, and the retry policy.
Predefine and deterministically implement feedback-intensity ablation levels; log and plan to publish complete verifier–planner exchange traces for reproducibility.
